title: IT Act s. 139 — Return of income (IT Act s. 139)

content.overview: Section 139 requires a person whose total income exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to tax to file a return. Specified companies, firms and other persons file even below that amount where the section says so. Belated, revised and updated returns are permitted only within the enacted windows. A return is not an assessment. The duty follows the section, not a notice. A notice can additionally require a return.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: The duty follows the section, not a notice. A notice can additionally require a return.
essentialIngredients: Income above the exemption limit, or a compulsory class
Belated or revised return only in its window
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 139(1) is the ordinary return. The due date differs for a company, a person whose accounts are audited, and others. A belated return is allowed up to the enacted date. A revised return corrects a filed return within its window. An updated return is a later paid return on the conditions in the section. Loss returns must be filed on time if the loss is to be carried forward, subject to the enacted exceptions.
examples: A person above the exemption limit does not wait for a notice.
A company files even at a loss if the section requires it.
A correction after filing is a revised return, not a second original return.
